text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99_stream_latency_us-west-2 > 4s for 7m on hosted-api-prod. Affected endpoints: /chat/stream, /v1/stream. Rule: streaming_p99 > 2.5s (7m window). Paging oncall.

mia (oncall): Acknowledged. Kicking off triage. Quick checks: dashboards, pod queue lengths, recent deploys, autoscaler events.

rafael (infra): Looking at infra graphs: p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 4.2s, CPU spiky on ~10% of pods. Autoscaler shows backpressure last 8m. Link: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/streams?from=now-10m

kara (runtime): Not seeing increase in errors. Logstream reveals long GC pauses in some worker JVMs at ~02:05 UTC. We applied kernel patch opt-3 last night. Could be interacting with GC/scheduling for short-lived streaming sessions.

mia (oncall): Rolling mitigations: 1) enable streaming-circuit-breaker to drop or short-circuit extremely long-running streams, 2) scale pool +50%, 3) reduce batch_window for streaming. Which is safe to do now?

rafael (infra): Scaling now. `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/hosted-streaming --replicas=16` (from 11). Should be up in ~40s. ops-bot will confirm.

ops-bot: autoscaler override: scaled hosted-streaming 11 -> 16 (requested by rafael).

kara (runtime): I can flip `streaming.circuit_breaker=true` to prevent runaway sessions and set `batch.window_ms=5` for streaming lanes. Pushing flags now:
```
redwoodctl set-config streaming.circuit_breaker true --env=prod
redwoodctl set-config batch.window_ms 5 --env=prod --scope=streaming
```
Propagation ~8s.

mia (oncall): Good. Also create routing bypass for us-west-2 to send 30% of new streams to us-west-1 dedicated fallback. `redwoodctl route modify`?

rafael (infra): Applied smart-routing: fallback:dedicated-us-west-1 weight=0.3 for streaming. ops-bot: confirm.

ops-bot: routing update accepted; traffic shift ~28% over 60s.

kara (runtime): After flags, initial metrics: p99 dropping to 1.9s, p95 steady. GC logs show fewer long pauses. However one pod still shows 6s stall; pulling logs.

mia (oncall): Any recent deploys or kernel rollouts near start time?

rafael (infra): Kernel/opt-3 rolled at 02:10 UTC to prod. Canary looked fine but traffic pattern different. I'll mark kernel rollout as suspected.

tom (customer-ops): Notifying CS for customers with >1% failed/very-slow streams in last 10m. Drafted message: "We're aware of elevated streaming latency in us-west-2; mitigations in progress; we'll update in 30m."

deploy-bot: deploy(runtime-service) rollback requested by kara: rollback to commit 1b2c3d. CI checks queued.

kara (runtime): Rolling back runtime change that included opt-3 kernel flag and minor batching tweak. Starting rollback now; will post when complete.

deploy-bot: rollback to 1b2c3d started. Estimated completion 90s.

mia (oncall): Monitoring after rollback. If p99 normalizes then root cause likely kernel-opt interaction. Also capture flamegraphs for the stuck pod.

ops-bot: rollback succeeded; runtime-service now at commit 1b2c3d.

kara (runtime): Post-rollback check: p95=330ms, p99=870ms, error-rate normal. Flamegraphs show sys CPU spike pre-rollback. Stalled pod recovered.

rachael (infra): (typo earlier) confirming no pending autoscaler interference.

mia (oncall): Handoff plan: I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand to kara for postmortem and RCA. jen? (Note: jen not present)

tom (customer-ops): Sent customer update: initial mitigation implemented, rollback deployed, we will follow up with root cause. Customers acknowledged.

kara (runtime): Action items: collect heap/GC traces for affected pods, run short-prefix streaming regression across canary + rollback builds, schedule postmortem. I'll own the RCA.

mia (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated at 1779054705. Will keep open for 1h monitoring. Incident ID INC-2026-1779054321.

incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-1779054321. Severity: Sev2. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/streaming-latency-runbook

(End of thread)
